+# to be success, then runs origin/main's copy of the check again, because a pull_request run
+# executes the PR's own copy of this file and of the script. The job name IS the context, and

+# the triggers and permissions below.

+# connector review; a submitted or dismissed review is what changes its findings. Never
+# `labeled`, `unlabeled` or `edited`: that fan-out cost txe 3.2 runs per push on the review
+# gate. So adding `review-override` runs nothing by itself: re-run this check after adding it.
+#
+# THE POLL. A clean connector pass edits its summary comment and reacts, and neither fires an
+# event here, so a pull_request run waits for the state block to reach the head (every 30 s, up
+# to 15 min) instead of failing minutes before the connector finishes. That holds one light
+# runner for the connector's latency, 3 to 4 min per pass on txehq/sub2api PR 290. A
+# pull_request_review run decides at once: the review it was started by is already there.
+# Drafts are skipped: the connector does not review a draft, and GitHub does not merge one.
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    types: [opened, synchronize, ready_for_review]
body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Revalidate the gate when the base branch changes**

When an already-green PR is retargeted from another branch to `main`, its effective diff can expand without changing `.head.sha`; [GitHub explicitly warns that changing the base can make existing review comments outdated](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/pull-requests/how-tos/create-pull-requests/changing-the-base-branch-of-a-pull-request). Because `edited` is excluded here and both the check script and `merge-pr.sh` validate the connector state only against the unchanged head SHA, the old `codex-review` success can authorize merging code the connector never reviewed. Trigger and invalidate/review on base changes, or bind the gate evidence to the reviewed base/diff as well as the head.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep polling after unrelated review events**

If any human submits or dismisses a review while the connector is still processing a new head, this `pull_request_review` run cancels the existing polling run via the workflow concurrency group and then checks immediately because the wait is zero.
